content.text: can we make the pi's settings.json writable temporarily

Assumption: `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` is Home Manager-managed and symlinked into the Nix store. I’ll locate its declaration, make the smallest change that produces a writable copy, then run the repository validator. “Temporarily” will mean until we revert this config change.

input.command:
printf 'PI vars:
'; env | rg '^PI_' || true; printf '
Current settings path:
'; ls -l ~/.pi/agent/settings.json 2>/dev/null || true; stat -f '%Sp %N' ~/.pi/agent/settings.json 2>/dev/null || true

content.text: The config already has writable-copy behavior for work machines, but this host intentionally uses a Home Manager symlink. For a genuinely temporary change, no repository edit is needed: I’ll replace only the current symlink with a writable copy. The next Home Manager/Darwin activation will restore the managed symlink.

input.command:
set -euo pipefail
settings="$HOME/.pi/agent/settings.json"
tmp="$(mktemp "$HOME/.pi/agent/.settings.json.XXXXXX")"
cp -L "$settings" "$tmp"
chmod 644 "$tmp"
mv -f "$tmp" "$settings"
ls -l "$settings"
stat -f '%Sp %N' "$settings"
test -f "$settings" && test ! -L "$settings" && test -w "$settings"

content.text:
Done. `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` is now a writable regular file.

The next Home Manager/Darwin activation will restore the Nix-managed symlink. No repository files were changed.
